# Project Information {#projinfo}

## Objectives:
 
 
  * Analyze two groups of samples:
    
    + Nicotiana tobacum and 
    + Petunia hybrida

  * No. of samples: 12 x2 ( 4 groups; 3 replicates each)
  
  * Groups to compare: all vs all
 
  * Obtain a list of the differentially expressed gene in each development stage and compare it between each of the 4 stages 
 
  * Comparison to arabidopsis: Identify homologs of those differentially expressed genes in Arabidopsis.
  
  Note: Letter corresponds to species, T=tobacco and P= Petunia, first number: dev. stage (1, 2, 2.5 or 4), last number: replicate, numbers range from 1 to 6 but only 3 are submitted per stage:
T1.1; T1.2; T1.3; T2.1; T2.2; T2.3; T2.5.1; T2.5.2; T2.5.3; T4.2; T4.3; T2.4
P1.3; P1.4; P1.5; P2.1; P2.2; P2.3; P2.5.1; P2.5.3; P2.5.4; P4.1; P4.3; P2.6





# Petunia hybrida RNA seq analysis {#petunia}

## Preprocessing and Quality check {#qc.pet}


###   Reference Genome


 FASTA: Petunia_axillaris_v1.6.2_genome.fasta
 
 GFF: Petunia_axillaris_v1.6.2_gene_models.gff                  
 
 
 Source : [https://solgenomics.net/organism/Petunia_axillaris/genome](https://solgenomics.net/organism/Petunia_axillaris/genome)



###  FASTQC Output of the raw reads


```{r,echo=FALSE,eval=FALSE}
dir.create("Result_Analysis_Petunia/01_fastqc_report",showWarnings = TRUE, recursive = TRUE)
suppressMessages(library(fastqcr))


##-- Run fastqc on raw reads or trimmed reads and place it the folder 

# Using bash script to get fastqc report.
# make sure you have GNU parallel installed in machine.
# > find -name "*fastq.gz" | parallel fastqc {} -o 01_


# Demo QC dir

qc.dir <- c("Result_Analysis_Petunia/01_fastqc_report/")
qc.files <- list.files(qc.dir, full.names = TRUE)

qc <- qc_aggregate(qc.dir)
library(dplyr)
ok<- qc %>%
  select(sample, module, status) %>%    
  filter(status %in% c("WARN", "FAIL")) %>%
  arrange(sample)


# Inspecting QC Problems
#%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

# See which modules failed in the most samples
#qc_fails(qc, "module")
# Or, see which samples failed the most
#qc_fails(qc, "sample")

# Building Multi QC Reports

qc_report(qc.dir, result.file = "Result_Analysis_Petunia/01_fastqc_report/multi-qc-report", preview = FALSE)
```

```{r}
pca.ap[, "RepID"] <- anno$RepID

j = 2

png(file = file.path(
  figdir,
  paste0(figcount[cnt], "PCA_sample_group.png")
),width = 10, height = 8,units = 'in', res = 300)

ggplot(pca.ap, aes(
  x = eval(parse(text = paste0("PC", i))),
  y = eval(parse(text = paste0("PC", j))),
  colour = Group,
  #   shape = RepID
)) +
  geom_point(stroke = 1.5,
             size = 3,
             alpha = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#a6611a",
                                "#dfc27d",
                                "#80cdc1",
                                "#018571"
  )) +
  
  # scale_color_manual(values = c("dodgerblue3","seagreen2","firebrick3","#E69F00", "darkmagenta", "#ea10c9")) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(1,2,3,4)) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = RepID),
    size = 4,
    check_overlap = FALSE,
    nudge_y = 3
  ) +
  xlab(paste0("PC", i, ": ", round(perc_pc[[i]], 2), "%")) +
  ylab(paste0("PC", j, ": ", round(perc_pc[[j]], 2), "%")) +
  #theme_bw(base_size = 15)  +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(color = "grey20", size = 20, angle = 90, hjust = .5, vjust = .5, face = "plain"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(color = "grey20", size = 20, angle = 0, hjust = 1, vjust = 0, face = "plain"),

  # Change the appearance and the orientation angle
  # of axis tick labels
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(face="plain", color="black",
                                   size=14, angle=0),
        axis.text.y = element_text(face="plain", color="black",
                                   size=14, angle=90)) +
  
  
  
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA),
    panel.background = element_blank(),
    axis.line = element_line(colour = "black"),
    axis.line.x= element_line(colour = "black"),
    axis.line.y.left = element_line(colour = "black")
  ) + theme(aspect.ratio = 1)
```

```{r}
#create contrast list
contrast_list <- c("PhyII_vsI", "PhyIII_vsI","PhyIV_vsI","PhyIII_vsII","PhyIV_vsII","PhyIV_vsIII")

#DEG RAW for  all 6 comparison

for(y in 1:6){ #Loop through the  six comparisons
  
  # RES1 
  res1<-
    data.frame(topTable(
      efit,
      coef = contrast_list[y],
      adjust = "BH",
      n = nrow(dge$counts)
      # sort.by = "none"
    ))[, c("Symbol", "logFC", "P.Value", "adj.P.Val")]
  
  
  colnames(res1) <- paste( colnames(res1),contrast_list[y], sep = ".")
  
  write.csv(
    res1,
    file = file.path(tabdir, paste("Table",contrast_list[y],"_DEG_TotalValidGenes_in_Genome.csv",sep="_")),
    quote = TRUE, row.names = F
  )
  
  
  write.table(
    rownames(res1),
    file = file.path(tabdir, "genenames_DEG_TotalValidGenes_in_Genome_GO_bg.txt"),
    col.names = F,
    row.names = F,
    quote = FALSE,
    sep = "\t"
  )
  my_contrast_list[[y]] <- res1
}
```

### Volcano plot


Comparison  of all 6 contrasts

```{r}

#####volcano plot####
volcano_panel <- list()
for ( z in 1:6){
  # fig1
  # z =2
  gene_list = my_contrast_list[[z]]
  #gene_list[is.na(gene_list)] <- 1
  gene_list$color_flag <-
    as.factor(
      ifelse(
        gene_list[2]< -log2FCcutval  &
          gene_list[4]< aPVALcutoff,
        "Downreg",
        ifelse(
          gene_list[2]> log2FCcutval  &
            gene_list[4]< aPVALcutoff,
          "Upreg" ,
          "Non-DE"
        )
      )
    )
  
  colnames(gene_list)<- c("Symbol","logFC","P.Value","adj.P.Val","color_flag" )
  gene_list$gene_names <- gene_list$Symbol
  #gene_list[!gene_list$Gene_Symbol %in% rownames(deg[1:30,]), "gene_names"] <- ""
  
  #convertlofFC to FC
  
  
  volcano_panel[[z]] <-  ggplot(data = gene_list,
                                aes(
                                  x = logFC,
                                  y = -log10(adj.P.Val),
                                  colour = color_flag
                                )) +
    #, label = gene_names
    geom_point(size = 0.75) +
    # geom_text(size=2, color="black", hjust=0, vjust=3, aes(logFC,-log10(P.Value),label=gene_names)) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-10, 10), ylim = c(0, 9)) +
    labs(title=paste(contrast_list[z]), x ="Fold-change (log2)", y ="P-value (-log10)") +
    xlab("Fold-change (log2)") +
    ylab("P-value (-log10)") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("dodgerblue4", "gray", "firebrick4")) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA),
      panel.background = element_blank(),
      axis.line = element_line(colour = "black")
    ) +
    theme(aspect.ratio = 1) + theme(legend.title = element_blank())
  #  geom_text_repel(size = 2.5, color = "black")
  
}
```

```{r}
##### heatmap####
##################################################################
exp <- v$E
colnames(exp) <- paste0(colnames(exp), "_", anno$Condition)


cnt <- cnt + 1
for (p in 1:6) {
  deg.genes <-
    read.table(file.path(tabdir, paste0("genenames4_GO_deg_", contrast_list[p], ".txt")), header = F)
  print(nrow(deg.genes))
  deg <-
    exp[rownames(exp) %in% deg.genes[, 1], grep("_", colnames(exp))]
  
  deg <- t(scale(t(as.matrix(deg))))
  mtscaled <- deg
  dim(mtscaled)
  hc = hclust((dist(mtscaled)), method = "ward.D")
  
  col = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))
  png(file.path(figdir, paste0(figcount[cnt], "heatmap_avgExpr_", contrast_list[p], ".png")),width = 10, height = 8,units = 'in', res = 300)
  hm <-
    heatmap.2(
      mtscaled,
      labCol = anno$IDs ,
      symm = F,
      scale = 'none',
      main = paste0("Heatmap: ", contrast_list[p]),
      ylab = paste0("FC > ", FCcutoff, " ;  adj.Pval <  ", aPVALcutoff),
      cexRow = 0.75,
      cexCol = 0.75,
      trace = "none",
      dendrogram = 'column',
      Rowv = as.dendrogram(hc),
      #Colv = T,
      col = col(24),
      symbreaks = T,
      srtCol = 45,
      labRow = FALSE
    )
  dev.off()
}
```

```{r}
#####logCPMheatmap####

lcpm <- cpm(dge, log = T)
cnt <- cnt + 1
newcnt2 <- cnt

for (i in c(1:6)) {
  Cntrl_vs_Treatment <- topTreat(efit, coef = i, n = Inf, sort.by = "P")
  Cntrl_vs_Treatment.topgenes <- rownames(Cntrl_vs_Treatment)[1:25]
  var1 <- which(row.names(v$genes) %in% Cntrl_vs_Treatment.topgenes)
  #  mycol <- colorpanel(1000,"blue","white","red")
  col = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))
  deg <- lcpm[var1, ]
  deg <- t(scale(t(as.matrix(deg))))
  mtscaled <- deg
  dim(mtscaled)
  hc = hclust((dist(mtscaled)), method = "ward.D")
  
  #rownames(mtscaled) <- mapIds(org.Mm.eg.db, rownames(dge), column="ENTREZID", keytype="ENSEMBL") 
  png(file.path(
    figdir,
    paste0(figcount[newcnt2], "heatmap_top25_logCPM", colnames(efit$contrasts)[i], ".png")
  ),width = 10, height = 10,units = 'in', res = 300)
  heatmap.2(
    mtscaled,
    labCol = anno$IDs ,
    symm = F,
    main = paste0("Heatmap: ", colnames(efit$contrasts)[i]," FC > ", FCcutoff, " ;  adj.Pval <  ", aPVALcutoff),
    xlab = "logCPM HeatMap",
    #  title  = ,
    scale = 'none',
    cexRow = 0.75,
    cexCol = 0.75,
    trace = "none",
    dendrogram = 'none',
    Rowv = as.dendrogram(hc),
    Colv = F,
    col = col(24),
    symbreaks = T,
    srtCol = 45,
    margins = c(8, 10)
  )
  dev.off()
}
```

# Methodology {#methods}

<br>

### Differential expression analysis:


Adaptor sequences and low-quality score containing bases (Phred score < 30) were trimmed from reads using Trimmomatic (Bolger, Lohse, and Usadel 2014). The resulting reads were aligned to the  Petunia axillaris and Nicotiana tabacum genome, using STAR (Dobin et al 2012). Read counts are obtained using HTSeq (Anders et al 2015). The R package limma (Ritchie et al 2015) was used to identify differences in expression levels between the groups. Nominal p-values were corrected for multiple testing using the Benjamini-Hochberg method. Arabidopsis homologs for each gene was obtained using BLASTP (Camacho et al, 2008)

<br>
 

### Gene Ontology (GO) and KEGG enrichment analysis:

We considered all the genes which were differentially expressed. Functional enrichment analyses (Gene Ontology and KEGGs) were performed with gProfileR (Reimand  et al 2009). Enrichment p-values were based on a hypergeometric test using the set of known human genes as background.  The default “g:SCS method “ was applied for multiple testing correction.  It corresponds to an experiment-wide threshold of a=0.05, i.e. at least 95% of matches above threshold are statistically significant.
 
<br>
